title: 2003 AMC 10B Problem 8
statement: The second and fourth terms of a geometric sequence are \(2\) and \(6.\) Which of the following is a possible first term?

solutions.text:
Let the terms be \(a,\) \(ar,\) \(ar^2,\) \(ar^3,\) \(\dots\) with \(ar=2\) and \(ar^3=6.\) Dividing gives \(r^2=3,\) so \(r=\pm\sqrt3.\)

Then \(a=\dfrac{2}{r}=\pm\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}=\pm\dfrac{2\sqrt3}{3}.\) The choice \(-\dfrac{2\sqrt3}{3}\) matches the negative case.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Dividing the fourth term by the second term gives \(r^2\)
With \(ar=2,\) the first term is \(a=\dfrac{2}{r},\) and \(r\) may be negative
